entities.name: Methyl ester hydrolysis
observations: Reactant contains –CH2–C(=O)OCH3; product contains the corresponding –CH2–C(=O)OH while the rest of the scaffold is unchanged.
The decoded molecular formula changes from C31H35N3O5 to C30H33N3O5, consistent with replacement of methoxy by hydroxy and loss of methanol-equivalent carbon/hydrogen.
Most plausible reaction class is ester hydrolysis, commonly performed by aqueous base followed by acidification or by aqueous acid.

entities.name: Aqueous base saponification
observations: Plausible conditions include LiOH, NaOH, or KOH in aqueous alcohol such as THF/water, methanol/water, or ethanol/water, followed by acidic workup to give the carboxylic acid.

entities.name: Acidic ester hydrolysis
observations: Alternative conditions include aqueous HCl or H2SO4, often in water, methanol, ethanol, or mixed aqueous solvent, with heating as needed.
